transcript.content: hey, I'm Berry. if there's a dream you remember, even just a scrap of it, I'm here to listen.
hey Berry. there is one bit that keeps coming back to me, from last night. it was snowing inside the office, at my desk.
snowing inside. at your desk. that's odd and kind of lovely.
yeah, it was really soft somehow. like the whole room went quiet and white. nobody else even looked up.
you were the only one who noticed.
right. everyone just kept typing. the snow was piling up on the desks and keyboards, all over the carpet. it covered everything.
and it covered you too?
I don't really remember it landing on me, though I suppose it must have. what I remember is the office turning white, like only the tops of the monitors were still showing.
so the room changed while you were just there in it. did it feel more like you were yourself sitting at the desk, or like you were seeing it from somewhere else?
I felt like I was still me, sitting there, but kind of outside it too somehow. it was peaceful. I wasn't worried at all.
peaceful and outside it, while the snow kept coming down. what happened next?
my manager Dele came over to tell me something. he's a tall man in a blue suit. but while he was talking he turned into a snowman, still wearing the suit and holding his coffee mug.
the snow swallowed him and he just went on with it.
almost. it wasn't like the snow swallowed him, more like he just became the snowman. still standing there with the mug, like nothing had happened.
so the office starts turning to snow from the inside out. did that make it feel any different, or was it still peaceful for you?
still peaceful. I made a snowball after that, and it glowed a bit in my hand. that's the last thing I remember before I woke up.
a glowing snowball. that's quite an ending.
yeah, it was. I don't know what it meant, but it felt right.
some things in dreams don't need to mean anything, they just land right. you said it's the bit that keeps coming back to you.
exactly. it was all soft and watery, like a watercolour painting with the colours bleeding into each other. that’s the feeling I keep holding onto.
soft and watery, colours bleeding. that's a lovely way to carry it.
it really is. I'd like to see it drawn, actually. you know, if someone could get that feeling.
that sounds possible. before we get there, tell me something about that watercolour feeling if you don't mind. did it sit more in the ways things moved, or more in how the place looked?
I'd say more in how the place looked. the slow big flakes made it feel like that too, but it was mostly the way everything blurred at the edges.
so the edges softened, and the shapes kind of merged into one another. that's the look of it.
yes, that's exactly it. like nothing had a hard line.
nothing hard-edged in any of it. what about the thing that's stayed with you the most since you woke up?
the snowman in the blue suit still holding his coffee mug. that's the image I keep seeing.
that image, the man in the suit who'd become snow, still holding his mug.
yeah. it might sound silly, but that one frame felt the most calm.
it doesn't sound silly at all. calm in the middle of something so strange.
right. and maybe that's why I can still see him so clearly.
maybe so. you remember him as holding the mug and standing there, like normal, but he's snow. what do you remember about his face, in that moment?
I don't remember his face, actually. just the shape of him, and the suit, and the mug.

it was snowing inside your office. big soft flakes, everything quiet and white. nobody else looked up, they just kept typing. snow piled on the desks and keyboards, and the room turned white. you felt peaceful, like you were sitting there but also outside it. then your manager dele, tall in his blue suit, came over and turned into a snowman still holding his mug, like nothing had happened. you made a snowball and it glowed a little in your hand. it all looked soft and watery, like a watercolour with colours bleeding into each other, edges blurred. the part that stays is that snowman in the suit, no face, just the shape and the mug, and how calm it felt.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. that's the whole thing, the way I remember it.
then would you like to see it drawn?
yes, I really would.
which of these feels closest to you? or would you describe it another way?
the watercolour one, where the edges blur and everything runs into everything else. that's how it felt.

watercolour it is.

I'll start with dele. I picture him as a tall man in a blue suit, holding his coffee mug. since you don't remember his face, i'll leave that part soft and unfinished, just the shape of him. those are my guesses from what you told me. is there anything you'd change, or should i leave it like that?
leave it like that. the face being soft and unfinished fits.

i'm sketching dele and the office and the coffee mug and the snowball now. it'll appear on the right. that's all i'm drawing for the moment.

i'll draw you too, since you're in it. would you like me to draw you as you are, or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me. the dream didn't show me what I looked like in it.

i'm sketching you now.

everything's being drawn and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. once it's there, you can say if anything looks wrong.

they're on the right? let me look.

the office with the snow everywhere, that one looks right. the screens poking out above the white. and dele as a snowman in the blue suit with the mug, that fits too.

the watercolour feel is there in most of them. I'd maybe want the edges even softer, more blurring into each other, but it's close.

i'm glad the office and dele feel right to you, and the softer edges note makes sense.

does it look the way you remember, overall?
overall, yeah. it looks right. the office and dele especially. the one where the room turned white, with the screens just poking out, that's very close to how it felt.

that's lovely to hear. the room turning white with the screens just poking out, that feels like the moment the dream turned soft.

the other drawings are still on their way, they'll show up on the right soon. you can take your time with them.
okay, I'll wait for them. the screen one is the strongest for me, I think.

the screen one has a quiet power to it, the way the white takes over and only the tops of the screens remain.

the other drawings are still coming together, they'll be on the right soon.
alright. I think the snowball one might be interesting once it shows up.

the snowball glowed a bit in your hand, didn't it. that feels like a little pocket of something.

it should be on the right any moment now, along with the others.
I only see one new one so far, the snowball, I think. it looks right, glowing softly in my hand.

the snowball is one of the moments still being drawn, right now the one that's up is the snow falling inside the office and piling up on the desks.

does that one look the way you remember?
oh, okay. the snow falling inside with it piling on the desks, yes that looks right. it has that quiet feeling.

that quiet feeling is the heart of it, isn't it.

the other three moments are still on their way and should show up on the right soon.
yes, that's the heart of it. I see a second one now, dele turning into the snowman. that looks right too.

glad dele turning into the snowman feels right to you.

the new one that's up is you sitting at your desk while the snow fills the room. does that look the way you remember?
I see it now. me at the desk while the snow fills the room. that looks right, though I don't really know how I looked in it, so I'll say it fits.

that's you sitting at your desk while the snow fills the room, and I'm glad it feels right even if you couldn't see yourself in it. the other two moments are still being drawn and will be on the right soon.
